fragments: Say what your character is trying to do. Roll when the outcome is uncertain. Keep this handbook beside your character sheet during play.
Choose a pregenerated character. Say what you try; use your sheet's values.

STR (Strength): power. CON (Constitution): endurance. DEX (Dexterity): coordination. SIZ (Size): height and bulk. INT (Intelligence): reasoning. POW (Power): will. CHA (Charisma): magnetism and leadership.
Skill %: test target; at 60%, roll 60 or less unless it Fumbles.
HP: current / maximum Hit Points; injury lowers current HP.
MWL: Major Wound Level; the damage from one hit that wounds you.
Combat Order: add to 1D10 when combat starts.
DM: Damage Modifier; add to melee, unarmed and thrown damage, not bows, crossbows or slings.
AP: Armour Points, subtracted after Parry.
ENC: equipment burden. Armour ENC also reduces Combat Order.
Hero Points: spendable chances to change an outcome.
HP 8/12: 8 current, 12 maximum. MWL 6 stays 6 when you lose HP. Use armour-adjusted Combat Order; do not subtract its ENC twice. Ask if your pregen does not say whether armour is included.
Rolls 3-4 · Skills 5 · Combat 6-11 · Ranged 12-14 · Intimidate 15 · Wounds and help 16-17 · Equipment 18-22.
Say what you want to achieve and how you try. Roll when uncertainty, pressure or danger makes failure matter. Routine and impossible actions need no roll.
Choose two ten-sided dice: tens and units. Set Bonus/Penalty dice first (page 4). Read the examples above; two zeros mean 100, never zero.
Check Fumbles first: they override success. Skills cannot exceed 100%.
Critical: 01 through one tenth of your skill, rounded down. Any skill above 0% has at least 01 as a Critical; a 0% skill has none.
Success: at or below your skill, without a Critical or Fumble.
Failure: above your skill, without a Fumble.
Fumble: 99 or 100 below 100% skill; at 100% skill, only 100.
A Critical achieves your intent exceptionally well. A Fumble fails with a serious, risk-related consequence. Combat Criticals: page 8. Lower is not always better: compare grade first (page 4).

2D6+2: total two six-sided dice, then add 2. D gives the die's sides. Distances use metres; a grid square may represent 2 m. Round ordinary fractions to the nearest whole number, halves up. The Critical threshold specifically rounds down.
Bonus dice keep the better result; Penalty dice keep the worse. Your skill and Critical range do not change.
ONE UNITS DIE: 5 · TENS: 2 AND 6 · CANDIDATES: 25 / 65
Choose grade first. Within the same successful grade, the higher result wins an opposed test.
Cancel +B and -P one for one; keep at most +3B or -3P.
Roll one units die, one tens die, and an extra tens die per remaining Bonus or Penalty die. Pair every tens die with the same units die; 00 is still 100.
Choose by grade first: Critical > Success > Failure > Fumble. Within the same Critical/Success grade, higher is better; within Failure/Fumble, lower is better. Penalties reverse the choice.
Both choose their result, then compare grade, number and unmodified skill. An exact tie goes to the defender.
Deception 42 Success beats Perception 31 Success: same grade, higher number. Ordinary attacks use attack-then-Reaction (page 7); grappling is opposed.
Useful, timely help gives +1B total, not per helper. Assistants normally need 26% or more in the relevant skill. Exceptional combined help may give +2B.
Use your sheet's percentages. Routine competent work with time and suitable tools usually needs no roll.
Dodge: evade a perceived attack or physical hazard.
Persistence: resist intimidation, coercion and fear.
Resilience: endure fatigue, shock, deprivation, poison and disease.
Close Combat: attack and Parry with melee weapons and shields.
Ranged Combat: shoot or throw weapons at distant targets.
Unarmed Combat: punch, kick and grapple.
Culture: a society's history, geography, customs and beliefs.
Language: communicate; 50% gives fluent everyday speech.
Lore: specialist knowledge; successful preparation can give +1B to one directly related test soon afterwards.
Natural Lore: nature, tracking, weather, food and shelter.
Athletics: balance, climb, jump, run, swim and exert force.
Craft: make and repair goods in a chosen trade.
Deception: sneak, disguise, misdirect, conceal and pick pockets.
Driving: handle carts, wagons and similar vehicles.
Engineering: design, build, repair or sabotage large works.
Healing: stabilise, treat injuries and perform Surgery (pages 16-17).
Influence: persuade, bargain, command and intimidate.
Mechanisms: locks, traps and intricate devices.
Perception: notice hidden things, details and danger.
Performance: act, dance, sing, speak or play music.
Riding: control a mount in challenging circumstances.
Sailing: operate boats and ships under oar or sail.
Streetwise: urban rumours, contacts, illicit goods and discreet routes.
Trade: appraise value and negotiate a sale.
Craft subjects, Cultures, Languages and Lore fields are separate skills.
One round is five seconds. Close is within 2 m; farther away is Ranged.
At combat start, roll 1D10 + Combat Order; highest acts first. Ties go to higher DEX; if DEX also ties, those characters reroll 1D10 between them. Example: die 7 + Combat Order 12 = 19.
Combat Action: attack, start/escape a grapple, Aim, Set Weapon, Intimidate, or use a skill/object that takes about five seconds.
Movement Action: move up to Movement in metres, stand, drop prone or disengage. Leaving an enemy can trigger an Opportunity Attack (page 10).
Base Reaction: when eligible, Dodge, Parry or make an Opportunity Attack, even outside your turn. It interrupts only to resolve its trigger.
Combat and Movement Actions happen in Combat Order. Unspent actions never carry into the next round. You must still have every Action or Reaction an option spends or gives up before you choose it.

Use Movement Action to ready one item or nock an arrow while moving no more than half Movement. Stow one and draw another, or ready two items: use the whole Movement Action. Crossbow reload costs are separate (page 20).

Delay your Combat Action until after a chosen participant later this round. To interrupt an action already beginning, oppose the relevant skills; winner acts first. Delaying never creates an extra action.
Attack first; an aware defender may React after a hit. Not an opposed test.
ORDINARY PARRY AGAINST A HEAVY ATTACK
Roll Close Combat, Unarmed Combat or Ranged Combat. Success hits; failure misses. Check Criticals and Fumbles normally (page 3).
Melee or unarmed: Dodge normally, or Parry with a ready weapon or shield.
Ranged: Dodge at -1P. A ranged Parry uses Active Guard (page 13), with different choices for thrown weapons and projectiles.

An ordinary successful Dodge avoids the hit. You must perceive it and be able to move. Dodge only once per round, using your base Reaction. Parry uses Close Combat, or Unarmed Combat against an unarmed attack.
A failed Reaction changes nothing. One Reaction per attack or trigger. An unaware defender cannot React. Critical attacks use page 8.

Sizes ascend: Light, Medium, Heavy, Huge. Against an ordinary hit, a Parry of the same/larger Size blocks all; one smaller blocks half; two or more smaller blocks none. Then apply armour. Unarmed attacks are Light.
A Critical Parry blocks all damage regardless of Size.
When an adjacent enemy disengages or creates a clear opening, spend an eligible Reaction on one Close Combat attack. It grants no extra off-hand attack.
Resolve the Reaction before reducing HP. Critical attacks change damage and defence, not the number of attacks you make.
ORDINARY HEAVY HIT · MEDIUM PARRY · LEATHER ARMOUR
Parry first, armour second. Only the remaining damage reaches HP.
Roll weapon damage; add applicable DM and declared action damage; apply Parry, subtract AP, then lose the remaining HP. Damage and current HP cannot fall below 0. Round halves up.
DM applies to melee, unarmed and thrown damage, including negative DM. Bows, crossbows and slings use their listed damage.
None, failed or fumbled Reaction: roll damage, then armour. Successful Dodge: no damage. Ordinary Parry: reduce by Size, then armour (page 7). Critical Dodge or Parry: no damage.

No Reaction, failed or fumbled Reaction: maximum weapon damage plus maximum positive DM when normally added; ignore armour. Ignore negative DM and all other bonus damage, including the extra Charge die.
Ordinary successful Dodge or Parry: roll normal damage and apply armour. The Reaction neither stops nor reduces the hit.
Critical Dodge or Parry: no damage; Critical Parry ignores Size.
A Critical gives no free attack or manoeuvre. A Fumble brings a consequence suited to the risk, such as dropping a weapon or losing your footing. After HP loss, check Major Wound and 0 HP (page 16).
Two ready one-handed items give one extra option per round. Attack OR defend.
EXTRA DAGGER ATTACK -1PBASE SHIELD PARRY: NO OFF-HAND PENALTY
Weapon + weapon; weapon + shield; weapon + free hand; two bare hands. An empty hand counts as ready; a punch or kick can attack. A two-handed item does not qualify: it leaves no free hand.

After a standard Close Combat or Unarmed Combat attack, immediately make one free attack with the other item, or unarmed with a free hand, at -1P. Spend no Action or Reaction; add DM to both attacks normally. The first attack does not need to hit.

Keep the other item for one additional Parry or Opportunity Attack at -1P. This extra Reaction cannot Dodge. Your base Reaction remains available with either choice; a base shield Parry has no inherent off-hand penalty. Other situational penalties still apply.

Using either extra option locks out the other until next round. An Opportunity Attack, Charge or Set Weapon attack never produces an extra off-hand attack. Forfeiting all Reactions also removes the extra Reaction. Only one Reaction answers any one attack.
You must still have every listed Action and Reaction available.
SET WEAPON: ATTACK FIRST +1BCHARGE HIT: +1D6 DAMAGE
Disengage: Movement Action to leave; an enemy in reach may make an Opportunity Attack.
Withdraw: Combat + Movement Actions; move normally without those Opportunity Attacks. Keep your base Reaction.
Combat + Movement Actions: move up to twice Movement. Keep only your base Reaction, and use it only to Dodge.
Combat + Movement Actions; forfeit all Reactions. Move 5 m to twice Movement in a straight, clear route, end adjacent, then attack. A hit adds +1D6 damage. No other movement or off-hand attack.
Combat Action to set a ready Set-tagged weapon. A Charge into reach before your next turn triggers one Close Combat attack at +1B before the Charge.
It works once. Any Action, Movement Action or Reaction before the trigger unsets it.
Use this when you want to grab and hold someone, not injure them.

Choose an adjacent target and commit one free hand. An aware target may spend one eligible Reaction before opposing your Unarmed Combat with Dodge or Parry. Dodge uses the base Reaction, once per round. Parry uses Close Combat with a ready weapon/shield, or Unarmed Combat empty-handed.
Win to hold them. Without a defence Reaction, succeed at an unopposed Unarmed Combat test instead. A failed attempt leaves your hand free.

Neither participant can take a Movement Action, and both suffer -1P on every test. They may attack or Parry only with Unarmed Combat or a ready Light one-handed weapon. A hand used to hold cannot attack, Parry or count as an off-hand.

The held participant spends a Combat Action and wins Unarmed Combat versus Unarmed Combat; the controller's opposing roll costs no Reaction. The controller may release freely on their turn. Escape or release leaves both adjacent and frees the committed hand.
Only one controller can hold a target. The GM handles unusual Size, anatomy, footing and help.
Spend a Combat Action and test Ranged Combat. Cover modifies this roll; the defender reacts only after a hit.
Up to listed Range (R): normal. Beyond R through 2R: -2P. Beyond 2R: no shot. Shortbow: R = 75 m; 2R = 150 m.
Spend a Combat Action aiming at one visible target: +1B to your next ranged attack against it. Lose Aim on any Reaction, loss of sight, or failure to shoot with your next Combat Action.
Thrown weapons add DM and keep their listed Size. Bows, crossbows, and slings add no DM; their projectiles are Light.
Within 2 m, a Close-tagged ranged weapon can use Close Combat and its listed damage. Without that tag, it is an improvised Light club: 1D6 + DM, attacking at -1P.
Apply cover normally. An ordinary failure misses. Only a Fumble may hit a fairly or randomly selected nearby target: normal rolled damage, then armour.
Aim +1B and a low wall -1P cancel. Roll normally. If the attack hits, resolve the defender's Reaction separately.
Cover changes the attack. An aware defender may React only after a hit.
Partial (low wall): attack -1P. Substantial (battlements): attack -2P. Complete: blocked attack line, no attack. Cover absorbs no damage.
Dodge -1P: once per round, base Reaction only. Perceive the danger and be able to move away.
Test Close Combat with an eligible ready item:
Thrown weapon: ready weapon -1P; ready shield no guard penalty.
Arrow, bolt, or sling projectile: shield only, -1P.
Carrying a shield adds no attack penalty. A strapped shield cannot guard while you wield a weapon with both hands.
Ordinary hit: successful Dodge avoids it; successful Parry blocks by Size. Any ready shield fully blocks a Light projectile on success.
Critical hit: ordinary defence success means normal rolled damage after armour, with no avoidance or Parry reduction. Critical defence stops it, regardless of Size.
Extra off-hand Reaction: add -1P (shield vs arrow: -2P before other modifiers); cannot Dodge. One Reaction per attack.
Use these common modifiers. The GM handles unusual circumstances.
MELEE FROM ABOVE OR BEHIND: ATTACK +1B
Target moved since your last turn: 10 m or more -1P; 30 m or more -2P instead.
Target partly obscured by mist, smoke, fog or foliage: -1P; heavily -2P.
You are prone: -2P. You are on unstable ground: -1P.
You are engaged at Close range: -2P per enemy.
Range/Aim: page 12. Terrain cover: page 13. Obscurity is not cover. The GM handles wind and other difficult conditions.
Target prone, flanked or attacked from behind: attack +1B.
Higher ground: the advantaged attacker or defender +1B.
You are prone: melee attack or defence -1P.
You are on unstable ground: -1P to the affected test.
An unaware defender cannot React. Behind/beside does not automatically mean unnoticed. An alert defender can React to a rear attack; that attack gains +1B.
Use the strongest version of the same condition; combine different causes. Cancel +B/-P, then cap at +3B / -3P.
Combat Action: pressure an enemy to surrender or flee.
Choose one enemy or a group. State what you want them to do and make the threat clear.
Oppose your Influence against the target's Persistence. The GM decides whether the attempt is possible and applies any modifier.
If you win, the enemy may yield or flee; the GM describes the response. Intimidation creates pressure, not mind control.
One big hit can wound you. At 0 HP, help is urgent.
AFTER REACHING 0 HP: STABILISE BEFORE THE DEADLINE
One hit at least equal to MWL
After Parry/armour, one hit's damage at least equal to MWL causes a Major Wound. Apply HP loss and both conditions:
Wounded: -1P on every test. Bleeding: lose 1 HP at each round's end.
Conditions do not stack. Later Major Wounds deal damage and can restart Bleeding. No Resilience test or injury table. MWL 6: one 6 HP hit wounds; two 3 HP hits do not wound merely by totalling 6.
HP stops at 0. Die if still Dying at the end of the third Combat Round after reaching 0 HP. Stabilise before that deadline.
An adjacent helper spends Combat Action, Movement Action and all Reactions. Both remain stationary. Test Healing with a Healing Kit or suitable improvised supplies; -2P without them.

Success removes Bleeding and Dying, restores 0 HP, and leaves Wounded. Stable at 0 HP means unconscious. Stopping Bleeding does not unlock natural recovery from a Major Wound. Treatment and separate Hero Point protections: page 17.
Stabilise first (page 16). Treat the injury next. Hero Points are a separate choice.

Ordinary damage: after an encounter, a patient who is not Wounded may receive one Healing attempt before their next full rest. Success restores 1D4 HP, up to maximum. One attempt per patient, even if it fails.

Major Wound: once stabilised, successful Surgery (Healing, outside combat, safe conditions) restores 1 HP and unlocks natural recovery. A Wounded patient cannot heal naturally before Surgery or equivalent treatment. Ordinary treatment and Surgery suffer -2P without a Healing Kit.

Rest: no more than light activity restores CON / 4 HP per 24 hours, rounded nearest with halves up, never above maximum. After treatment, Wounded ends only when current HP > MWL. CON 14 restores 4/day; MWL 6 ends at 7+ HP.
Spend 1 Hero Point when declaring an effect
Try again: reroll a failed test, including a Fumble, after seeing it but before consequences or costs. The new result stands, even if worse. At most one reroll per test, regardless of source.
Downgrade a Major Wound: keep the full HP loss but prevent Wounded/Bleeding from that hit. It creates no Major Wound needing Surgery. Existing conditions remain.
Avoid Death: at 0 HP, become stable and unconscious, not Bleeding or Dying. Awaken after the scene at 1 HP; existing Wounded remains.
Story benefit: with GM approval, add a plausible favourable detail or coincidence. Larger benefits may cost several points; companions may contribute.
Separate effects: with 5 HP and MWL 6, taking 7 damage needs two points to both downgrade the Major Wound and Avoid Death. Mark spent points off your sheet.
Use Close Combat with held weapons; Unarmed Combat for punches/kicks. Add DM to damage. Below either STR or DEX minimum: attacks and Parries -1P, not -2P for both.

1H: one hand. 2H: two hands. Flex: two-handed use gives +2 damage and STR requirement 2 lower. Set: brace against a Charge (page 10). Thrown: use its ranged profile without an improvised-weapon penalty.
Size: determines Parry protection (page 7), not physical name or length. ENC: burden. SP: Silver Pieces. A dash means no listed value.
Two-handed longsword: 1D8 + 2 + DM, STR 11 / DEX 11. Still Medium; using both hands prevents off-hand options. More close weapons: page 19.
Add DM to listed damage. Below either STR or DEX minimum: attacks and Parries -1P; failing both still gives only -1P.

1H / 2H: one / two hands. Flex: two hands give +2 damage and a STR minimum 2 lower, without changing Size. Set: brace against a Charge (page 10). Thrown: use the ranged profile (page 21). SP: Silver Pieces. ENC: burden. Dash: no listed value.
Small shield is Medium; medium shield Heavy; large shield Huge. Compare these Sizes when Parrying, not the shield's everyday name (page 7).
Primitive or improvised versions of listed weapons deal 1 less damage, to a minimum of 1. A ranged weapon lacking Close has its own improvised use (page 12).
Ranged Combat; no DM. Below either STR/DEX minimum: attacks and Parries -1P; below both still only -1P.

Up to Range: normal. Beyond Range through twice Range: -2P. Farther: no attack. 1H / 2H: one / two hands. Missile: no DM. Arrows, bolts and sling projectiles are Light, despite launcher Size dashes. Aim: page 12.
Bow: nock one arrow with Movement Action while moving up to half Movement. A generic Ready action never shortens crossbow reload costs.
A small shield may be strapped to your arm while carrying a 2H ranged weapon, but cannot attack, Parry or provide Active Guard while you wield that weapon.
Per 10: arrows 1 SP; bolts 2 SP; sling bullets 5 CP. Bundles have no listed ENC. SP / CP: Silver / Copper Pieces. ENC: burden. Dash: no listed value.
Use Ranged Combat at distance. Below either STR or DEX minimum: attacks and Parries -1P, only once even if both are low.
THROWN DAMAGE ADDS DM; WHIP USES ITS OWN PROFILE

Thrown: ranged attacks add DM and retain the listed Size for Parry. Close: within 2 m, use Close Combat and the listed damage. Melee damage adds DM. A weapon without Close becomes an improvised Light club, 1D6 + DM, attacking at -1P when used within 2 m.
SP: Silver Pieces. ENC: burden. Dash: no listed value. Dagger melee requirements differ from this ranged profile; use the profile for the attack.

Up to Range: normal. Beyond it through twice Range: -2P. Farther: no attack. With STR 12, a javelin has 24 m Range: normal through 24 m, -2P beyond 24 through 48 m. Cover, Aim and defence: pages 12-13.
Subtract Armour Points after Parry. Armour never turns damage into healing.

Leather: padded, boiled leather or layered linen. Ringmail: sewn metal rings on padding. Scalemail: overlapping scales on padding. Chainmail: interlinked rings. Platemail: fitted steel plate over chain backing.
7 damage after Parry - 5 AP from Chainmail = 2 HP lost. Critical attacks have separate armour outcomes (page 8). Wearing multiple armours does not combine AP.

Armour ENC counts toward carried load and subtracts from base Combat Order. Use the armour-adjusted value on your pregen; do not subtract it twice. If equipment changes, update that value. SP: Silver Pieces.
SIZ 1-5: half listed cost and ENC.
SIZ 21+: double listed cost and ENC.
Ill-fitting plate: may be worn at double ENC. Other armour must fit well enough for the GM to allow it.
